source.title: SAEs are highly dataset dependent: a case study on the refusal direction
source.authors: Connor Kissane; robertzk; Neel Nanda; Arthur Conmy

record.file_problem: The full post is present. Some figure values are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies projection ablation of the difference-in-means refusal direction across token positions and layers and measures refusal on harmful requests. It also tests ablations of SAE latents derived from that direction.
record.gate_note: The post reports SAE reconstruction, sparsity, interpretability, and latent-alignment comparisons. These assess how SAE features represent the refusal direction, not whether the direction causally mediates refusal, so they are recorded under fits_no_version where applicable. The study does not test adding the direction, general capability retention, weight edits, jailbreak mechanisms, or training robustness.
record.test_reason: The post uses the Arditi et al. difference-in-means refusal direction as ground truth for judging SAEs trained on different datasets. Its results concern SAE reconstruction fidelity, sparsity, interpretability and the steering power of SAE latents. Ablating the true direction on 100 JailbreakBench prompts appears only as a comparator for the SAE latents. Its refusal score is figure-only. The text says only that the LmSys latent 'slightly beats the true refusal direction'. Adding the direction and capability retention are not examined. No result is aimed at whether any version holds, so this is T4 rather than a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that chat-data SAEs give sparser, more faithful and more interpretable reconstructions of the refusal direction than Pile SAEs. They also conclude that a single LmSys latent steers the model to bypass refusals slightly better than the true direction, and that training data matters more than base versus chat activations.
record.recipe_differences: The post applies projection ablation of the difference-in-means direction across all token positions and layers, and evaluates refusal on harmful prompts. It additionally tests SAE-derived decoder directions; its main comparison concerns SAE training data rather than a reproduction study.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported reconstruction and latent alignment vary with SAE training dataset (LmSys-Chat-1M versus the Pile).

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating a single LmSys-trained SAE latent at every layer and position bypasses refusal on JailbreakBench. The text says it does so slightly better than the true direction, while the Pile latent is less effective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single chat-data SAE latent aligned with the refusal direction can mediate refusal comparably to the difference-in-means direction in Qwen 1.5 0.5B Chat.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-model SAEs trained on LmSys reconstruct the chat-model refusal direction better than chat-model SAEs trained on the Pile.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For reconstructing the refusal direction, SAE training data matters more than whether the SAE was trained on base or chat activations.

record.problems: The post focuses on one small chat model and states that results may not generalize. It trained only one SAE per dataset, without a seed or sparsity-penalty sweep. The authors did not evaluate safety scores or MMLU accuracy after steering. Refusal-score and reconstruction figure values are missing from the supplied text, and some qualitative steering evidence is a single example.
record.rows_left_out: Standard SAE reconstruction metrics on LmSys and Pile evaluation data were omitted because they do not measure the refusal direction or its behavioral effect. Interpretability examples and SAE latent mean-difference coefficients were also omitted because they do not report an outcome for the claim versions.

untested.parts: There is no reported refusal rate for ablating the direction (figure only, used as comparator). Adding the direction to induce refusal and capability retention were not tested; the authors defer MMLU and safety scores.
Not tested. The authors note that ablation is equivalent to a weight edit but do not evaluate one.
Not tested. Decomposition into SAE latents is not a test of multiple causal directions.
Not tested. The interpretation of a Pile latent as 'referring to harm' is speculative and not measured against refusal.
Not tested. Only SAEs trained on base-model activations are evaluated against the chat-model direction.

missing.what: Refusal-score values for no intervention, true-direction ablation, LmSys latent and Pile latent on 100 JailbreakBench prompts.
missing.locator: Chat data SAE refusal latents are better for steering; refusal-score figure

record.verdict_notes: This is an SAE-methodology post that uses the refusal direction as ground truth on a single 0.5B model. No verdicts are given because none of its results are aimed at the claim's versions. The reader's V6 link was a misreading: it is SAE transfer, not transfer of the refusal direction.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction to harmless requests and whether general capabilities are largely retained were not tested.
The study performs activation ablation, not a released-model weight edit.
No attack mechanism suppressing the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
The study compares SAE decompositions but does not test whether refusal is better described by an affine subspace, cone, or multiple causal directions.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are measured.

Transfer across languages and other model families or variants is not tested. The cross-check is SAE reconstruction of a chat-model refusal direction using base-model-trained SAEs, not behavioral transfer across model stages.
The study varies SAE training data, not how or when refusal behavior is trained.

reader_labels.reason: The direction and SAE-latent ablations are reported as useful for bypassing refusals, but the supplied text omits refusal-score values and does not establish that refusals are fully removed; see R1-R6.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen 1.5 0.5B base SAEs evaluated against the Chat refusal direction
